neighbours.label: ' from' after keep or prevent in a physical explanation (keep the tiles from moving, prevent the vertebrae from grinding), as opposed to other uses of ' from' and ' keep'
fire: A rubber mat keeps the rug from sliding.
This bracket will prevent the shelf from tipping when loaded.
Pads prevent the bones from rubbing against each other.
The clip stops the cable from falling behind the desk.
Oil keeps the gears from grinding together.
Good seals prevent water from leaking in.
A spacer keeps the wheel from touching the frame.
Weights keep the tent from blowing away.
quiet: A rubber mat was bought from the store.
This bracket will look nice on the shelf when painted.
Pads were sent from the factory in boxes.
The clip came from a box behind the desk.
Oil prices rose from May to June this year.
Good seals live in water near the coast.
A spacer keeps a record of the wheel size.
Tents were borrowed from a neighbor.

notes: Peaks also on ' can' and ' will' in mechanical sentences (0.27, 0.32 in probes), not tested; maybe the pole is about mechanical failure.
